clue.text: Painting in water-colours

parts.note: read 'water-colours' as the colours of the ocean itself: a painting whose subject is the sea, not one made with watercolour paints

explanation.surface: A gallery label describing a picture done in watercolour paints.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture of the ocean is a marine painting, the waves and shore being the colours of the water.

clue.text: Put out about the doctor being gloomy

indicators.note: about means the annoyed word goes around the medical letters

parts.note: to be put out is to be annoyed or sore
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Someone is upset about their GP and feeling down.
explanation.definitionFit: Sombre means dark and dismal, melancholy in mood.

clue.text: Changes suit an American town

indicators.note: changes signals the letters of suit an are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A man swaps his suit in a US town.
explanation.definitionFit: Austin is the capital of Texas, a city in the United States.

clue.text: Game obtained by many a man with some craft

definitions.text: Game obtained by many a man with some craft

parts.words: Game obtained by many a man with some craft
parts.note: game suggests prey caught by skilled hunters; it is a board game won with pieces called men and some cunning

explanation.surface: Hunters with skill bag animals for the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A board game played with pieces called men, won by strategy and cunning.

clue.text: Knock up appropriate share

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for knock is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rap is a knock on a door
to appropriate something is to take it

explanation.surface: Wake someone and grab your fair portion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAP into PAR; 'appropriate' is a verb, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To partake is to take a share or portion of something.

clue.text: Quietly put on, though guarded

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quietly
to put something on is to add it, so added

explanation.surface: Someone stepped softly while staying on their guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though' is just a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something padded is cushioned and so protected against knocks.

clue.text: Bring together material for builders

explanation.surface: Gathering supplies for a building site.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggregate is to collect into a whole; aggregate is also crushed stone or gravel mixed into concrete.

clue.text: Quotidian recorders

parts.note: quotidian means daily; recorders suggests musical pipes or machines, but these people write down each day's events

explanation.surface: Ordinary everyday recording devices.
explanation.definitionFit: People who keep journals write an entry for each day.

clue.text: Scraping the bottom

parts.note: suggests scraping the barrel, desperation; here it is literally clearing mud from the bed of a river or harbour

explanation.surface: Being reduced to the very last resources.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing silt from a waterway's bed with a scoop or suction machine.

clue.text: They spend their days personally creating friction!

definitions.text: They spend their days personally creating friction!

parts.words: They spend their days personally creating friction!
parts.note: the surface suggests quarrelsome people stirring up trouble; the friction is literal rubbing, done by hand on a client's body

explanation.surface: A sly dig at awkward people who cause rows wherever they go.
explanation.definitionFit: Massage therapists work by rubbing the body with their hands all day.

clue.text: Turning brown in latter years, so it's related

indicators.note: the turned colour word is placed inside the word for years

parts.note: one's later years are old age, so age

indicators.note: turning means the colour word is read backwards here

parts.note: tan is a light brown

explanation.surface: Going brown in old age somehow makes one family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' makes NAT from TAN, and 'in' puts it inside AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnate is a kinsman traced through the male line, so a blood relative.

clue.text: Some of the cheaper articles seem inferior

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the cheaper articles seem are taken, a run within them

explanation.surface: Bargain goods appear to be of poor quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Less can mean lower in rank or importance, as in 'no less a person'.

clue.text: Re-establish control by the government

parts.note: a rein is a means of control, as in 'keep a rein on'
the state is the governing power of a nation

explanation.surface: A call for the authorities to take charge again.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone or something to a former position is to re-establish it.

clue.text: Watching a little jockey in great form

indicators.note: only a small part of the words jockey in great is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A racegoer looking at a small rider who is in fine fettle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' is racing language for a horse's or rider's recent record and merely dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Eying something means looking at it closely, keeping a watch on it.

clue.text: The lady made to work out

indicators.note: work out suggests sorting or reshaping, so the letters of made are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman is being sent to the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame is a title or term for a woman, often a lady of rank.

clue.text: Recognised way to order militia around

definitions.text: Recognised way to order militia around

parts.words: Recognised way to order militia around
parts.note: order around suggests bossing troops; here it is the standard parade-ground command for soldiers to face the opposite direction

explanation.surface: The accepted method of bossing soldiers about.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill command telling soldiers to turn and face the reverse way.

clue.text: Start sharing some with an old Greek

indicators.note: the start of the word sharing is just its opening letter

parts.note: a part is some of something

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek begins dividing things up with a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spartan was a citizen of Sparta, a city-state of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Secure leverage

explanation.surface: Getting a firm hold for a lever.
explanation.definitionFit: To purchase is to obtain or buy; purchase is also a firm grip giving mechanical advantage.

clue.text: Time a good man's taken-—the very least

parts.note: a minute is a short period of time
ST, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: The tiny amount of time a decent person has spent.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutest is the superlative of minute, meaning smallest or tiniest.

clue.text: Evening dress

parts.note: not formal wear for night-time, but clothing that evens everyone out by making them all look alike

explanation.surface: A dress code for a formal dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Regulation clothing worn by a group makes its members look the same, removing differences.

clue.text: A drink for

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'A drink for (4)' looks cut short in OCR; no parse gives the answer from these words alone.

clue.text: Through being without one gets support

indicators.note: being without here means standing outside, so the word for through wraps around the numeral

parts.note: per means through or by means of, as in 'per post'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Getting by without someone still earns backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking: PER goes around I.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a pillar or column that holds up an arch or bridge.

clue.text: The sack could mean medication over a period

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a pill is a tablet of medicine
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Getting fired could mean taking tablets for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, so pillage is looting.

clue.text: A green product that can cause anger

indicators.note: a product is something made, here the letters of a green worked into a new word

explanation.surface: An environmentally friendly item that annoys people.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrage is to make furious, to provoke rage.

clue.text: Given guidance about information? What a tale!

indicators.note: about means the guidance word is placed around the information word

parts.note: led means given guidance or guided
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Guided through the facts, someone marvels at the story.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British informal slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional story, a fable passed down.

clue.text: A yard is nothing in short!

indicators.note: the letter for nothing is set inside the word for short

parts.note: a curt reply is short and abrupt
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a yard counts for nothing in a brief measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A court is an enclosed open space, a courtyard.

clue.text: Sum granted to repair ocean wall

indicators.note: repairing means putting the broken letters of ocean wall back together in a new order

explanation.surface: Money is handed over to mend a sea wall.
explanation.definitionFit: An allowance is an amount of money given regularly, such as pocket money.

clue.text: Egghead's appearance after a scrap-quite pallid

indicators.note: after means the letter from the egg's head follows the scrap word

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, as in 'not a whit'
the head of the word egg is its first letter

explanation.surface: An intellectual looks very pale after a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' suggests an intellectual but gives just the E heading 'egg'; 'appearance' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: White describes a face drained of colour, ashen and pale.

clue.text: Approach for a rendezvous?

parts.note: a rendezvous is a meeting place, a venue

explanation.surface: Asking whether a certain route is the way to a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a way of approach, literally a tree-lined drive leading to a house.

clue.text: Trip as I'd leap fence

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the letters of as I'd leap fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A rider falls as they jump an obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A palisade is a barrier of pointed stakes, a defensive fence.

clue.text: One-time holiday accommodation area

parts.note: ex means former or one-time, as in ex-husband
a tent is camping shelter used on holiday

explanation.surface: A patch of ground once used for camping.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent is the size or area that something covers.

clue.text: Church man never badly taken in by the radical

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside the following word

parts.note: red is slang for a political radical or revolutionary

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of never are scrambled

explanation.surface: A clergyman who is never a bad sort is fooled by a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' turns NEVER into VEREN, and 'taken in by' sets it inside RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverend is the title of a member of the clergy, a minister.
